# Project Kestrel – Buyer-side review of Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**To:** Wattlebridge deal team | **Status:** Internal advice, privileged | **Basis:** Buyer Playbook; Seller documents treated as untrusted counterparty material

## 1. Headline

The Seller's package is not "fair and balanced" measured against our playbook. It departs on almost every negotiated limitation point, collapses the fundamental/title regime into the general regime, contains no fraud carve-out, and relies on whole-data-room disclosure plus a blanket buyer-knowledge bar. Several items the Seller describes as "addressed", "agreed" or "settled" are, on the Seller's own Disclosure Letter, not done at all (Bluefen consent, Riverlark release, DD-005 bonuses). Nothing in this package has been cleared through our authority process; in particular, **no Amelia Frost written approval exists** for the 20% cap or the 18-month period, so those remain at our starting positions.

Also note: the Disclosure Letter speaks as at **5.00pm 22 September 2026**. Today is 6 November 2026. Every factual statement below should be treated as potentially stale and refreshed before signing.

## 2. Issue-by-issue analysis

### 2.1 General Warranty cap (cl 12.1) – REJECT; hold 25% / AUD 6,000,000
Seller proposes 20% / AUD 4,800,000. That number happens to equal our conditional fallback, but the playbook is explicit: the fallback is usable *only* with prior written authority from Amelia Frost identifying the draft, and none has been given. A number matching a fallback is not clearance. Respond at 25% / AUD 6,000,000. If the team wants to consider moving, that is an escalation to Amelia Frost, not a drafting decision.

### 2.2 Thresholds (cl 12.2) – REJECT on all three elements
| Element | Seller | Playbook |
|---|---|---|
| De minimis | AUD 25,000 | AUD 5,000 |
| Basket | AUD 250,000 | AUD 50,000 |
| Recovery once exceeded | Excess only (deductible) | First dollar (tipping) |

The Seller's package is 5x our de minimis, 5x our basket, and converts a tipping basket into a deductible. Combined with the 20% cap this materially erodes real recourse. Counter at AUD 5,000 / AUD 50,000 / first-dollar.

### 2.3 Time limits (cl 12.3 / 13) – REJECT 18 months; DELETE "applies to all Claims" language
- 18 months is our fallback, but again requires Amelia Frost written approval, which has not been given. Hold at **24 months**.
- The proposal that "any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise" is a hidden general-regime override. It would sweep Title, Tax, IP, specific indemnities, payment and covenant claims into the general cap, basket and time bar unless we remember to carve each out individually. The playbook requires these categories to be kept separate. Reverse the default: general limitations apply **only** to general Warranty Claims; everything else is governed by its own regime.

### 2.4 Fundamental / Title warranties – REJECT
"Administrative simplicity" is not a reason to cap title and capacity at 20% for 18 months. Require a separate regime: **100% of price cap, minimum six years, outside the de minimis, basket and any knowledge qualifier**. This is a core protection on a 100% share acquisition and should be treated as non-negotiable.

### 2.5 Limitations, exclusive remedy, non-reliance (cl 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5) – REJECT; insert fraud carve-out
Applying these "to all Claims of any nature" contains no carve-out for fraud, wilful concealment or deliberate misconduct. The playbook requires those to be carved out of **all** caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance provisions to the maximum extent enforceable, and no one on our side may waive this. Also ensure exclusive-remedy does not cut across specific indemnities (Ironquay, bonuses, incident) or Completion covenants (Riverlark).

### 2.6 Disclosure (Schedule 7; Disclosure Letter paras 1.1–1.4) – REJECT general disclosure
- Para 1.1 discloses "every fact, matter and circumstance" in the data room; para 1.2 adds the Accounts, statutory registers and "publicly searchable corporate records". This is exactly the whole-data-room / public-register deemed disclosure the playbook rejects. Require **specific, fair disclosure** – i.e. disclosed with sufficient particularity to enable a reasonable buyer to identify the nature and scope of the matter – against identified warranties.
- Para 1.4 (nothing admits breach, liability, materiality or that any consent/payment/notice is required) is a standard non-admission, but combined with 1.1 it lets the Seller disclose problems without characterising them while still barring claims. Accept non-admission only if disclosure is specific.
- The specific disclosures (paras 2–10) are, to their credit, candid about gaps. We should use them: they are the Seller's own admissions that key conditions are unsatisfied.

### 2.7 Buyer knowledge (cl 8.3) – DELETE
Blanket exclusion for anything the Buyer "or its advisers had knowledge" of, including matters merely "discoverable" from the data room or public records. This is a constructive-knowledge bar that would gut the warranties. Delete entirely. If any knowledge concept survives, it must be: (a) actual knowledge of named Buyer individuals only (not advisers, not "discoverable"); and the Seller's warranties should be given on the basis of **named Seller knowledge persons after reasonable enquiry**. In no case may knowledge excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.

### 2.8 Bluefen consent (cl 3 / 6.3) – REJECT; hard Condition Precedent
Seller says the consent is "addressed" via reasonable endeavours and deemed satisfied on delivery of written consent. The Seller's own Disclosure Letter (para 2) confirms **no final written consent and no evidence that the cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied**. Bluefen is ~AUD 3.6m / ~30% of FY26 revenue – a material customer. Require:
- CP: Bluefen consent under cl 11.2 obtained, **effective** (not merely delivered), and **evidence that all cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied**, before Completion;
- Seller obligation to obtain, not merely reasonable endeavours;
- Buyer satisfaction right over the form of consent and any conditions attached.

### 2.9 Riverlark facility (cl 2 / 7) – REJECT post-completion release
~AUD 3.2m outstanding; change-control cl 8.1 and discharge cl 9.2 engaged. Disclosure para 3 confirms no repayment and no discharge. On a debt-free/cash-free deal we cannot take the Company with a live secured facility and a promised later release. Require:
- Current payout letter from Riverlark (refreshed to Completion);
- Repayment **directly from Completion funds** per the funds flow;
- Deed(s) of release and PPSR/other security discharges delivered **at** Completion.
Only if the bank cannot deliver releases at Completion: irrevocable undertaking from Riverlark to release on receipt of funds **plus** Amelia Frost approval. Absent that, this is a Completion deliverable, not a post-completion item.

### 2.10 Funds flow / DD-005 bonuses – REJECT "matter for the Seller"
AUD 420,000 of Completion-conditional bonuses are not in the funds flow and are described as the Seller's concern. They are not: the paying entity will be the Company, which we will own. Disclosure para 5 also admits silence on payroll tax, superannuation and other on-costs. Require either (a) a specific line item in the funds flow funded by the Seller (bonuses + superannuation + payroll tax + any other triggered on-costs), or (b) treatment as Debt / price deduction. Do not accept the "agreed price mechanics" characterisation – nothing has been agreed on this. Confirm whether any further bonus or change-of-control payments exist beyond DD-005.

### 2.11 Ironquay IP (cl 11.1) – BROADEN; verify the AUD 180,000
Seller's indemnity is limited to the SOW3 payment. The real risk is title to SOW3 Project Materials, which under DD-004 cl 7.3 transfers only on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. Position:
- Preserve the **cure**: Seller to procure payment of all outstanding SOW3 fees and a confirmatory assignment from Ironquay before Completion;
- Broaden the indemnity to cover any loss from defective title to, or third-party claims over, the Ironquay deliverables, not just the fee;
- The AUD 180,000 in DD-010 is an internal ledger figure, not independently verified in either direction – require bank evidence of payment or Ironquay's written confirmation of the balance.

### 2.12 Export/privacy incident (DD-006; cl 4.6 / Sch 6) – do not accept "not material"
The Seller's "not expected to be material" is an assertion, not a finding. Equally, nothing establishes a confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or any numeric exposure, and we should not assume one. Require:
- Pre-Completion covenant to preserve all logs and evidence, complete the investigation, and provide written updates (including the ~1,240-record scope, whether access occurred, and any notification analysis);
- A specific warranty/disclosure on the incident as at Completion;
- Reserve the question of a specific indemnity pending investigation outcome.

### 2.13 Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000; DD-008 / DD-011) – ASSESS, no automatic treatment
Seller calls these "ordinary-course operating costs". Disclosure para 8 states the data room does **not** say whether they are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course – so the Seller's label is unsupported. Playbook: no automatic Debt classification or price deduction. Action: diligence the three renewals together (timing, termination rights, whether already accrued at Completion) and decide treatment (ordinary course / working capital / Debt) on the facts.

### 2.14 Tax / IP – NOT settled; remain OPEN
The Seller's statement that tax and IP positions are "settled under the general regime" is a unilateral assertion. Playbook: these terms remain open, kept as separate categories, and nothing is agreed. Respond that Tax and IP warranties/indemnities are reserved and will be addressed separately; do not assume unlimited liability either.

### 2.15 Title – REJECT share register as sole evidence
DD-012 is a Company-maintained internal register supplied by the Seller. Playbook requires independent evidence. Require: current ASIC company extract and historical extracts, PPSR search against the Company and against the shares, Seller's constitution and board/shareholder resolutions evidencing authority, confirmation of no options, convertible instruments or pre-emptive rights, and share certificates/transfer at Completion. Disclosure para 10 itself concedes it "does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification".

### 2.16 Lower-order items
- **Office lease (DD-007):** notification obligation only; confirm the trigger and ensure notice is given pre-Completion; verify no change-of-control termination right.
- **Mossvale (DD-009):** assignment restriction; share sale likely not an assignment, but confirm no change-of-control clause and obtain comfort if the contract is material.
- **"Fair and balanced" / "agreed" / "addressed" / "settled":** none of these characterisations is accepted; per playbook sec 0.4 / 6.3, they carry no weight absent our own authority process.

## 3. Summary of recommendations

| # | Issue | Our response |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Cap 20% / AUD 4.8m | Hold 25% / AUD 6m; no Amelia Frost authority for fallback |
| 2 | Thresholds 25k / 250k / excess-only | AUD 5k / AUD 50k / first dollar |
| 3 | 18-month claims period | 24 months; no authority for 18 |
| 4 | "Limitations apply to all Claims" | Delete; general limits apply only to general Warranty Claims |
| 5 | Fundamental/Title in general regime | Separate regime: 100% cap, ≥6 years, outside basket/de minimis/knowledge |
| 6 | No fraud carve-out (9.3/12.8/20.5) | Carve out fraud, wilful concealment, deliberate misconduct from everything – non-waivable |
| 7 | Whole-data-room/public-register disclosure | Specific fair disclosure only |
| 8 | Blanket buyer-knowledge bar (8.3) | Delete; if anything, named Seller knowledge persons + reasonable enquiry; never for title/capacity/fraud/indemnities |
| 9 | Bluefen – reasonable endeavours, deemed satisfied | CP: effective consent + evidence 11.3 conditions satisfied pre-Completion |
| 10 | Riverlark – post-completion release | Payout letter, direct repayment from Completion funds, releases at Completion; otherwise irrevocable undertaking + Amelia Frost approval |
| 11 | DD-005 bonuses excluded from funds flow | Specific seller-funded line item incl. super/payroll tax/on-costs |
| 12 | Ironquay – narrow indemnity | Broaden to title/claims; preserve SOW3 cure; independently verify AUD 180k |
| 13 | DD-006 "not material" | Preserve logs, investigate, updates, bring-down disclosure; no assumption either way |
| 14 | Sandbar "ordinary course" | Diligence; no automatic Debt/price treatment |
| 15 | Tax/IP "settled" | Open; separate categories; reserved |
| 16 | Title via DD-012 only | Independent ASIC/PPSR/authority evidence |
| 17 | Disclosure date 22 Sept 2026 | Require refreshed Disclosure Letter and bring-down at Completion |

**Escalation items for Amelia Frost (decision needed only if the team wishes to move):** cap (fallback 20%), claims period (fallback 18 months), any post-completion Riverlark release. Default position absent her written instruction identifying the draft: hold all playbook starting positions.

Happy to turn this into a formal issues list / mark-up of the Seller Update and a response letter on the Disclosure Letter if that's the next step.

- Pre-Completion covenant to preserve all logs and evidence, complete the investigation, and provide written updates (including the ~1,240-record scope, whether access occurred, and any notification analysis);
- A specific warranty/disclosure on the incident as at Completion;
- Reserve the question of a specific indemnity pending investigation outcome.

### 2.13 Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000; DD-008 / DD-011) – ASSESS, no automatic treatment
Seller calls these "ordinary-course operating costs". Disclosure para 8 states the data room does **not** say whether they are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course – so the Seller's label is unsupported. Playbook: no automatic Debt classification or price deduction. Action: diligence the three renewals together (timing, termination rights, whether already accrued at Completion) and decide treatment (ordinary course / working capital / Debt) on the facts.

### 2.14 Tax / IP – NOT settled; remain OPEN
The Seller's statement that tax and IP positions are "settled under the general regime" is a unilateral assertion. Playbook: these terms remain open, kept as separate categories, and nothing is agreed. Respond that Tax and IP warranties/indemnities are reserved and will be addressed separately; do not assume unlimited liability either.

### 2.15 Title – REJECT share register as sole evidence
DD-012 is a Company-maintained internal register supplied by the Seller. Playbook requires independent evidence. Require: current ASIC company extract and historical extracts, PPSR search against the Company and against the shares, Seller's constitution and board/shareholder resolutions evidencing authority, confirmation of no options, convertible instruments or pre-emptive rights, and share certificates/transfer at Completion. Disclosure para 10 itself concedes it "does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification".

### 2.16 Lower-order items
- **Office lease (DD-007):** notification obligation only; confirm the trigger and ensure notice is given pre-Completion; verify no change-of-control termination right.
- **Mossvale (DD-009):** assignment restriction; share sale likely not an assignment, but confirm no change-of-control clause and obtain comfort if the contract is material.
- **"Fair and balanced" / "agreed" / "addressed" / "settled":** none of these characterisations is accepted; per playbook sec 0.4 / 6.3, they carry no weight absent our own authority process.
